subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Lesson 5: Vocabulary and Grammar – Extreme weather & reported speech
outcomes: Give safety tips for extreme weather.

tf.s: Thunder, lightning and flood are weather words in Khalid’s diary.
tf.why: Yes, Khalid’s diary also has storm, cyclone, wind and rain.

tf.s: A heatwave is a period of very cold weather.
tf.why: A heatwave is a very hot period of weather.

tf.s: “I asked my dad what a cyclone was” reports the question “What is a cyclone?”
tf.why: Correct! The question word stays and is becomes was.

tf.s: A reported question does not need a question mark.
tf.why: Right! It is a normal sentence: He asked me where I lived.

tf.s: “Sara asked me where I lived” is a correct reported question.
tf.why: Great! It has normal word order and a past verb.

tf.s: We use “if” to report a Wh- question.
tf.why: We use if for yes/no questions; Wh- questions keep the question word.

tf.s: “He told me not to panic” reports the command “Don’t panic!”
tf.why: Right! told + object + not to + verb.

tf.s: In reported questions, “is” usually changes to “are”.
tf.why: The tense moves back: is changes to was.

tf.s: The reported question “I asked my dad what was a cyclone” is correct.
tf.why: The correct order is: I asked my dad what a cyclone was.

tf.s: In a flood, you should walk in the water to get home quickly.
tf.why: You should go to a high place and not walk in the water.

boxes.q: What do we call a long time with no rain?
boxes.why: A drought means no rain for a long time.

boxes.q: Which comes from a mountain with fire and hot rock?
boxes.why: A volcano sends out fire and hot rock.

boxes.q: Which word reports a yes/no question?

o: Grandpa told us to get out.
Grandpa asked us if get out.

boxes.q: Report ‘Do you like heatwaves?’ (Bassam asked Talal)
o: Bassam asked Talal if he liked heatwaves.
Bassam asked Talal do you like heatwaves.
Bassam told Talal to like heatwaves.
boxes.why: Yes/no question: asked + if + past tense.

boxes.q: Weather with ice falling from the sky:
boxes.why: Hail is small balls of ice.

o: stay inside and close the windows
boxes.why: Staying inside keeps you safe from the sand.

o: I told you to close all the windows.
I told you closing all the windows.
I asked you if close all the windows.
boxes.why: Commands use told + object + to + verb.

boxes.q: Which word is a fire in a big area of trees?
Report ‘Where’s my book?’ (Samira asked her dad)
o: Samira asked her dad where her book was.
Samira asked her dad where is my book.
Samira asked her dad if where her book.
boxes.why: Keep the question word, change is to was, no question order.

hunt.q: Mountain with fire and hot rock
Too much water covers the land

mcq.q: Which word means heavy snow with strong winds?
mcq.why: A snowstorm is a storm with a lot of snow.

mcq.q: Which is the pattern for reporting a command?
Which pair of weather words came from Khalid’s diary?
mcq.why: Khalid’s diary had storm, thunder, lightning, cyclone and flood.

mcq.q: How do we report a Wh- question?
mcq.why: Example: I asked my dad what a cyclone was.

mcq.q: Report: ‘Do you know what to do?’ (I asked him)
o: I asked him if he knew what to do.
I asked him do you know what to do.
I told him to know what to do.
I asked him if did he know what to do.
mcq.why: Yes/no question: asked + if + past tense.

mcq.q: Report: ‘Look at my volcano poster.’ (Sara told the class)
o: Sara told the class to look at her volcano poster.
Sara told the class look at my volcano poster.
Sara asked the class if look at her poster.
Sara told the class to looking at her poster.
mcq.why: told + object + to + verb, and my becomes her.

mcq.q: Report: ‘Don’t start a forest fire!’ (He told me)
o: He told me not to start a forest fire.
He told me to not starting a forest fire.
He asked me if start a forest fire.
He told me don’t start a forest fire.
mcq.why: Negative commands use not to + verb.

mcq.q: Which is the best safety tip for a flood?
o: Go to a high place and don’t walk in the water.
mcq.why: High places keep you away from flood water.

mcq.q: Find the mistake: “Samira asked her dad where was her book.”
o: The word order: it should be “where her book was”.
mcq.why: Reported questions use normal sentence order.

mcq.q: Why do we say “I asked him if he liked it” and not “I asked him if he likes it”?
o: The tense moves back in reported speech.
We never use present verbs in English.
mcq.why: In reported speech the tense usually goes back, like is → was.
